name: InstaBox
oneLiner: Firecracker machines with a browser desktop, sold as a subscription that is also a monthly credit.
whatItIs: InstaBox sells full Linux virtual machines, one per AI agent, that boot in about a second, keep their disk between sessions, and can be paused with memory and running processes intact.

Each machine is a Firecracker microVM running Debian 13 with its own kernel, root, systemd and Docker. You drive it from a web dashboard, a CLI, a TypeScript SDK or plain HTTP, and you can watch or take over its graphical desktop.

The intended buyer is a team running coding or computer-use agents that needs a real machine per task, not a single shared dev box. InstaBox is not InstaCloud, InsForge's separate managed-backend product.
whoFor: Teams and individuals running agents that need a persistent, general-purpose Linux box with a browser and desktop, who are comfortable with a CLI or API.
isolation: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel, root and passwordless sudo. Docker works. Templates are versioned images; you cannot bring your own OCI image.
sizes: Fixed vCPU/RAM pairs by plan: Free is 4/8 only; Pro adds 2/4 and 8/16; Builder goes to 16/32; Team to 32/64. One disk at `/data`, 20 GiB by default, growable live to 200 GiB on Pro.

billing.model: Monthly subscription that is also a credit: $20, $100 or $500, reset monthly.
billing.meter: Per second while running, on the size you asked for: $0.004 per vCPU-hour, $0.00225 per GiB-hour, $0.00011 per GiB-hour of storage, $0.02 per GiB of egress.
billing.stopped: Storage only. Paused and stopped machines pay GiB-hours for their disk and snapshots; paused memory is not billed and does not count as stored data.
billing.planFee: The plan fee is the credit. Usage comes out of it first, then pay-as-you-go, and unused credit expires at month end.
billing.minimum: $20 a month on Pro, or the free plan: one 4/8 machine, five snapshots, 100 GiB of egress a month.

A.headline: $3.20 of usage, billed at $20 on Pro
A.shape: 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 20 GiB disk, deleted after each task (Pro or above)
notes: The $20 plan is also $20 of credit, so the bill is the plan price.
On Free the 2/4 size does not exist; the nearest 4/8 would be $5.67 of usage, billed at $0.
A.flag: The free plan is 4 vCPU / 8 GiB only, so this workload cannot run there as specified.

B.headline: $28.84 a month
notes: The vendor's calculator shows $24.82 because it leaves storage out of the total.
Always-on needs the idle pause turned off, which paid plans allow.

C.headline: $3.14 of usage, billed at $20 on Pro
notes: On Free the nearest size would be $4.67 of usage, billed at $0.
A free machine pauses itself after 30 idle minutes and cannot run more than 8 hours continuously.

usability.dashboard: Yes, a full console: create a machine from a template with a button, start/stop/pause, open the Computer tab to click the Linux desktop, publish ports, save snapshots from the Playground, read metrics and billing.
usability.withoutCode: Partly. Creating a machine, opening its desktop, using Chromium, publishing a port and saving a snapshot are all click-driven. Claude Code and Codex are preinstalled, so you can type a plain-English request into the box's terminal. There is no hosted agent product and no prompt-in, result-out API.
usability.signup: GitHub or Google. Whether a brand-new free account needs a card is not published: the pricing page says $0, while the API has a `cardMissingAt` state that blocks free machines. Paid plans subscribe by card in the dashboard.
usability.docs: 26 pages, each available as Markdown, plus an `llms-full.txt` bundle; every page states limits and failure modes. Support is email on paid plans, priority on Team, and there is a Discord. No public status page was found.
tripsUp: The quick start is a terminal command, `npx instabox@latest sh`.
Two different off switches: pause keeps the session, stop does not, and you cannot stop a paused machine.
A snapshot does not save the session, only files and installs.
Fork is not instant, despite the homepage.
The free machine is not a server: it pauses after 30 idle minutes and cannot run longer than 8 hours.
Public port URLs have no password.

caveats.issue: The homepage says a fork copies running processes; the docs say otherwise
caveats.detail: Marketing says fork a machine mid-run and copy a running machine in seconds, listing Running Processes. The docs say fork is snapshot save plus create, and a snapshot does not hold memory or running processes.

caveats.issue: The free plan's 8-hour continuous runtime cap is only in the API schema
caveats.detail: `MaxRunMinutes` defaults to 480 for free machines. No docs page mentions it, so a reader of the pricing page would not know.

caveats.issue: Docs and API disagree on whether a preview visit wakes a paused machine
caveats.detail: The ports page says a visit wakes an idle-paused machine; the OpenAPI says preview links remain offline until resumed.

caveats.issue: Whether the free plan needs a card
caveats.detail: The pricing page says $0 and Get started; the API has a card-missing state that makes free sandboxes answer 402. It may apply only to workspaces that once had a paid plan.
Home is `/data/home`, so saved GitHub, Claude, Codex, git and SSH logins travel into every machine built from a snapshot.

caveats.issue: No published regions and no status page
caveats.detail: The Terms say the United States; there is no region selector. status.instabox.sh does not resolve.

strengths: A dashboard that creates a machine and opens a clickable Linux desktop.
Pause that keeps memory and running programs, billing storage only.
Org Secrets in proxy mode: the machine holds a placeholder, not the key.
Cheap per-hour rates: $0.004 per vCPU-hour and $0.00225 per GiB-hour.
Computer-use MCP and human takeover of the desktop, with control handed back.
